name: PlugTheHole Mail Log
author: PlugTheHole

sections.description:
PlugTheHole Mail Log records outgoing WordPress emails in a clean admin table. It is designed for short-term troubleshooting, clear support checks and privacy-conscious WordPress sites.

Features include:

  • Outgoing email logging.
  • Failed email logging.
  • Status filter and search.
  • Popup email preview.
  • CSV export.
  • Daily retention cleanup.
  • Admin-selectable short-term retention of 7, 14 or 30 days.
  • Manual cleanup button.
  • Single and bulk log deletion.
  • Resend to original recipient without creating a new log entry.
  • Clear all logs with confirmation.
  • Optional privacy mode to avoid storing message previews.

Optional Pro Add-on

PlugTheHole Mail Log is fully functional on its own. A separate PlugTheHole Mail Log Pro add-on is available from PlugTheHole.com for sites that need additional team, monitoring and troubleshooting tools.

The separate Pro add-on includes advanced search, saved searches, failure alerts, audit logging, role-based access controls, advanced exports, custom redaction, retention profiles and email test tools.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugthehole-mail-log plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate PlugTheHole Mail Log in WordPress.
  3. Go to Mail Log in the admin menu.
  4. Review the settings and choose the retention period that fits your site.
sections.faq:
Does this store full emails?

It stores a safe preview by default. You can turn preview storage off in the settings.

Does it store attachments?

No. It only stores attachment names.

Does this prove an email was delivered?

No. It records that WordPress attempted to send the email through the normal WordPress mail system. Inbox delivery still depends on your mail server, SMTP setup, DNS records and the recipient mail system.

How long are logs kept?

The default is 7 days. Site admins can choose 7, 14 or 30 days in the plugin settings. Shorter retention is recommended for privacy and database size.
